ai.title: What objective is reasoning solving?
ai.summary: Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.

ai.title: Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling

There are two types of test-time scaling: one allows researchers to trade more compute for more performance per task, but only up to the maximum quantity of per-task compute used during training; and the other lets researchers trade more compute for more performance per task, and lets them do so up to quantities of compute and performance that never occurred during training. Scaling methods that permit the latter change will have a larger impact than test-time scaling considered simply. This essay describes how this may impact the world.

infosec.title: Trusted by Default: Qubole Cross-Account Access Abused in the Wild
infosec.summary: From October 14 to 26, an attacker used IAM credentials from Qubole's AWS account (805246085872) to assume the cross-account roles customers had set up to trust the vendor. It then harvested Secrets Manager, SSM, and Lambda secrets, checked them against AWS, Entra ID, and Okta using TruffleHog, and downloaded entire S3 buckets. Most of the roles it assumed had no legitimate Qubole activity that month, and every request included a valid External ID. Customers should search CloudTrail for AssumeRole calls from that account originating from non-AWS IPs or with quiam-* session names, delete unused vendor roles, and pin trust policies to the vendor's principal using an aws:SourceIp condition, which alone would have blocked every attempt.

infosec.title: Detecting and Responding to AI-Aided and Agentic Attacks
infosec.summary: Distinguishing between human behavior, humans assisted by LLMs, and autonomous agents is critical to identifying the type of adversary behind an attack. LLMs can adapt to new information and carry out operations quickly, but they may make mistakes when generating synthetic headers or exhibit coding antipatterns, such as switching frameworks or using input and output handling that is more machine-friendly than human-friendly. Agents may also use a map-reduce-like pattern: they fan out information-gathering tasks, then synthesize the results all at once.

infosec.title: Contagious Interview: One Interview Away From Infection
infosec.summary: JFrog followed a single malicious npm package to AccuraSoftHire (accurasofthire[.]com), a fake company with job ads on Indeed and LinkedIn, ID-verified recruiter profiles, and a React take-home test. The test's Tailwind config loads one look-alike forms plugin carrying a loader that runs when the CSS builds, not at npm install, so install-script scanners never see it. Whenever npm removed that plugin, the operator republished it under a new name, and the careers site's "video verification" step was rigged to fail so it could push a curl one-liner that downloads a fake "camera driver."

infosec.title: PHP2Shell — Deep Dive
infosec.summary: PHP2Shell is a use-after-free chain that can lead to remote code execution. A crafted multipart request triggers an out-of-memory condition during session.upload_progress processing. PHP's bailout path skips cleanup, leaving stale global pointers in a long-lived worker process. A later request reclaims the freed memory and forges a zend_string length field, causing PHP to return 256 bytes of nearby heap data in a Set-Cookie header. The attacker extracts heap and code pointers, defeats ASLR, forges a HashTable, hijacks pDestructor, and executes a command. The article demonstrates an exploit that targets PHP 8.4.26 Alpine CLI and depends on precise heap grooming.

They also proposed a batch-factoring method that could make each additional 1024-bit key about 30 times cheaper to factor, though it remains unimplemented. The signature attack needs roughly 4 billion signing queries and does not recover private keys. Modern systems using 2048-bit or larger RSA keys are unaffected.

marketing.title: Yahoo's Economists Ran 25 Ad Experiments and Could Not Tell Profit From Loss
marketing.summary: Yahoo's research shows that most advertising lift tests lack the statistical power to distinguish profitable campaigns from unprofitable ones, even when they reach millions of people. Its 25 experiments found that the median confidence interval for ROI exceeded 100 percentage points, making it difficult to separate real impact from normal sales fluctuations. Instead of running many small tests, allocate testing budgets to the two or three channels that account for most of your spend, and run larger, longer, repeated experiments. Before launching a test, define its minimum detectable effect and report the confidence interval alongside the estimated lift. Treat results that cannot reliably detect meaningful returns as directional signals, not proof that a channel works.

crypto.title: Walraswap: Equilibrium-Based DEX Integrating External Liquidity
crypto.summary: Walraswap proposes an equilibrium-based batch DEX that integrates external AMM liquidity, where a price vector exists such that all submitted orders execute with no token deficit or surplus. Unlike CoW Swap, UniswapX, and 1inch Fusion, which use uniform clearing prices alone, Walraswap's equilibrium property requires including all available trade orders, closing the solver manipulation vector where order censorship shifts clearing outcomes. DAO-elected solvers retain censorship as the sole attack surface, which the protocol treats as detectable in a repeated game (analogous to block builders not unbundling searcher bundles). The construction, originating at Flashbots in 2023, frames settlement as a convex optimization problem. Net trades at equilibrium are unique despite non-unique price vectors.

crypto.title: Block Time and PropAMMs: From Ethereum to Base Denim
crypto.summary: PropAMMs face a core execution risk: the gap between an onchain quoted price and the live market rate spans one block, letting fast traders extract value at the maker's expense during that window. On Ethereum's 12-second blocks, builders such as Titan address this by guaranteeing a maker's latest price update lands before any competing trade in the same block, a mechanism Flashbots is standardizing as ERC-8324 and that Fermi has used to process hundreds of millions in weekly DEX volume. Base's Denim upgrade converts each 200ms flashblock slot into a full block, retiring the preview layer, shrinking the staleness window from 2 seconds to 200ms, and giving aggregators and solvers fresher quotes up to 2 seconds sooner. For propAMM operators, Denim makes per-block exposure limits more precise and shifts the execution advantage from tip size to sequencer latency, a dynamic Biconomy has been testing with a major market maker on its own Base propAMM since October.

All decisions and reviews funnel into a single prioritized queue with screenshots and video demos per feature, cleared in batches by voice and keyboard shortcuts. crypto.title: Where onchain credit fits in the AI boom
crypto.summary: AI compute is now a debt business, with 110 public GPU financings totaling $197B since 2023, mostly led by big banks that only serve borrowers large enough to justify diligence. That leaves small neoclouds underserved, and USD.AI lends to them from stablecoin deposits against GPUs as collateral, at 10-15% rates (12% median) versus 9-10% fixed at banks, and says loans can clear in under 7 days. It has originated $531M across 20 financings, and its sUSDai vault targets a 7% yield. The new GLX program sells seasoned loans so the cash can be re-lent, and the first exit was the $98.1M Duos Edge AI loan, repaid within four months. CHIP buybacks are funded by the protocol's 10% cut of interest, and onchain lenders hold under 1% of the $48.4B GPU debt raised in 2026. Risks include fast GPU depreciation, neocloud consolidation, and a mismatch between 30-day withdrawals and roughly 3-year loans.
